name: Classical
description: Classical and early-20th-century piano repertoire and composers.
curatedFacts: Chopin wrote most of his music for solo piano — unusual even among Romantic composers.
Debussy's "Clair de Lune" is the third movement of his Suite bergamasque, begun around 1890 and revised before its 1905 publication.
Erik Satie marked his scores with instructions like "play like a nightingale with toothache."
The modern piano has 88 keys; Beethoven wrote for instruments with as few as 61.
Rachmaninoff could reportedly span a thirteenth on the keyboard — about 12 inches.
Scott Joplin's "Maple Leaf Rag" was published in 1899; its first print run of 400 copies took a year to sell.
Bach, Mozart and Beethoven were all celebrated as keyboard improvisers.
